'''Abo Shrine''' (あぼじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located along the {{ill|Kamikawa River|Q11589669|qid=Q11589669}} in {{ill|Kamikawa, Saitama|Q1346757|qid=Q1346757}}, {{ill|Kodama District, Saitama|Q938038|qid=Q938038}}, {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|Q128186|qid=Q128186}}. The enshrined deities are six in number: Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, Susanoo-no-Mikoto, Izanami-no-Mikoto, Ninigi-no-Mikoto, Ōmiyanome-Ōkami, and Furu-Ōkami. It is a disputed candidate for the Shikinaisha minor shrine “Imajo Aozaka Inami Shrine” of {{ill|Musashi Province|Q907398|qid=Q907398}}, {{ill|Kami district|Q11634927|qid=Q11634927}}. Its former shrine rank was village shrine.

=== History ===
In Enryaku 3 (784), {{ill|Abo no Asomi Hitokami|Q50641391|qid=Q50641391|lt=Abo no Asomi Hitokami}} of Abo Village in {{ill|Iga Province|Q1047128|qid=Q1047128}} founded “Imajo Aozaka Inami Shrine.”
The village name “Abo Village” is said to derive from a village of the same name in his home province; the shrine name “Imajo” refers to the construction of a single fort, and “Aozaka” is said to originate from the sound-similar word “ao” (blue) to Abo. <ref name="今城青坂稲実池上神社明細帳">From the old document “Meisaichō” of Imajo Aozaka Inami Ikegami Shrine</ref>
Abo no Asomi Hitokami later became “Governor of Musashi” (provincial governor of Musashi Province) on the 8th day of the 8th month of Enryaku 5 (786),<ref name="続日本紀延暦五年八月甲子">From the entry for the 8th month, kinoshi day, Enryaku 5 (786) in *Shoku Nihongi*: “Junior Fifth Rank, Upper, Abo no Asomi Hitokami appointed Governor of Musashi.”</ref> and on the 6th day of the 2nd month of Enryaku 9 (790) he became “Director of the Imperial University” (equivalent to a modern university president).<ref name="続日本紀延暦九年七月戊子">From the entry for the 7th month, tsuchinoe-ne day, Enryaku 9 (790) in *Shoku Nihongi*: “Junior Fifth Rank, Upper, Abo no Asomi Hitokami appointed Director of the Imperial University.”</ref>
In Jishō 4 (1180), {{ill|Abo Sanemitsu|Q11450275|qid=Q11450275|lt=Abo Jirō Sanemitsu}} constructed the shrine buildings.

In Tenshō 5 (1577), Sekiguchi Village was separated from Abo Village. Sekiguchi Village transferred the “Niu Shrine,” which had been enshrined behind “Rokusho Myōjin Shrine” (this shrine), from Abo Village to Sekiguchi Village and made it the tutelary shrine of Sekiguchi Village (present-day “Imajo Aozaka Inami Ikegami Shrine”).

In Bunsei 1 (1818), villagers rebuilt this shrine, which had fallen into ruin. During the Edo period, the shrine was known as “Rokusho Myōjin Shrine.”
On May 3, Meiji 43 (1910), the Inari Shrine at Inari-juku, which was regarded as a disputed candidate for the Shikinaisha “Imajo Aozaka Inami Aramitama Shrine,” was merged into this shrine, and the shrine name was changed to the current “Abo Shrine.”

'''Shrine rank'''
* Kyōhō 12 (1727) – Senior First Rank (Rokusho Daimyōjin)
* Taishō 5 (1926), December 23 – Shrine authorized to receive offerings of sacred food and ritual implements

=== Enshrined deities ===
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto}} (おおなむちのみこと)
* {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}} (すさのおのみこと)
* {{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}} (いざなみのみこと)
* {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Q1056017|qid=Q1056017|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto}} (ににぎのみこと)
* {{ill|Ōmiya-no-Me|Q24865597|qid=Q24865597|lt=Ōmiyanome-Ōkami}} (おおみやのめ)
* {{ill|Futsu-no-mitama|Q11059754|qid=Q11059754|lt=Furunomitama-Ōkami}} (ふるのみたまのおおかみ)

=== Subsidiary shrines ===
* Kofumine Shrine
* Tenmangū
* Kokage Ōkami, Shinmei Shrine, Inari Ōkami, Hakusan Shrine, Yasaka Shrine, Jūniten Shrine

=== Access ===
* From the bus stop “Tanshō Station” at JR Hachikō Line Tanshō Station, take the Asahi Bus “Honjō–Jinsen Line.” Get off at “Moto-Abo” bus stop and walk 20 minutes.
* From JR Takasaki Line Honjō Station, take the Asahi Bus “Honjō–Jinsen Line.” Get off at “Moto-Abo” bus stop and walk 20 minutes.
